features.contract: Unique persisted stage tokens fence every application, recovery and rollback; policy authority is checked inside the same TradingDesk.set_book SQL write transaction. Exact token-qualified policy history recovers committed effects without replay over newer operator policy.
1–12 predefined read-only nodes, ordered backward-only dependencies, immutable canonical plan hash, 900–604800-second cadence, at most four scheduled enqueues and one executed node per pass.

Persisted 120-second node lease and unique token prevent duplicate commit after cancellation or supersession. Only source collection, provider bars, read-only catalogue lookup and factual dependency summaries are exposed; no shell, orders or policy tools.

Failed node blocks pending run nodes; explicit retry resets failed/blocked nodes but retains attempts and immutable prior receipts. Summary consumes completed dependency results and carries original plan hash.

Run cancellation persists terminal run/node state and clears active leases; in-flight result cannot produce a workflow receipt. Disabling workflow changes future cadence only. Underlying read-only collectors can finish their own source receipts/cache while workflow result is discarded.

def _record(self, sym, kind, source, payload, source_time=None):
        encoded = json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), allow_nan=False)
        sha = hashlib.sha256(encoded.encode()).hexdigest()
        rid = hashlib.sha256((sym + kind + source + sha).encode()).hexdigest()
        with self.store.transaction() as con:
            con.execute("INSERT OR IGNORE INTO research_receipts VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)", (rid, sym, kind, source, source_time, now(), encoded, sha))
        return {"id": rid, "kind": kind, "symbol": sym, "sha256": sha}

features.contract: Source receipts are hash-addressed; HTTP bounded to 8 seconds/2 MB; each pass collects two due symbols; catalogue opens SQLite mode=ro with literal query bindings. Research export includes workflow runs/nodes/receipts.

Research router exposes register/configure/run/retry/cancel and node-result routes; app binds Lab and Research into runtime and joins snapshots/export. Actual HTTP tests pass with isolated DB and workers disabled.

findings.title: Workflow accepted provider-unsupported bar parameters
findings.baseline: max/1h registered then provider rejected; workflow validation had a separate inconsistent allowlist.
findings.fix: Use actual provider BAR_DAYS and BAR_INTERVALS; 1h rejected at registration. Current provider max support exists; no claim max is currently invalid.

findings.title: Stale retained provider cache recorded as completed research node
findings.baseline: Provider result stale_cache=true and error was accepted because workflow checked only stale.
findings.fix: Explicitly reject stale_cache along with stale and empty bars.

findings.title: No explicit run cancellation endpoint
findings.baseline: Disabling cadence left queued execution active and no cancellation API existed. Disable behavior now explicitly documented as future cadence only.
findings.fix: Durable run cancellation clears tokens and all pending/running nodes; late commits discarded.

findings.title: Expired old apply caller can change policy after operator rollback
findings.reproduction: Pause apply before trading.set_book; force stage_until=0 to model a still-live caller whose 120-second grace expired; observer resets applying to approved; operator rollback changes stage to rolled_back; resume old set_book. Final stage stays rolled_back yet fees become 2. This is an isolated NEW-code test with fake interruption and no broker calls.
findings.expected: Stale/withdrawn application must be fenced before policy effect commits, in same policy transaction.
